Help & Clinical Explanations Time in Range (TIR) The percentage of time your glucose stays within your target range (70–180 mg/dL or 3.9–10.0 mmol/L). Clinical consensus recommends aiming for > 70% in range, < 4% low, and < 1% very low. Glucose Management Indicator (GMI) Calculates an estimated laboratory HbA1c based on your continuous glucose average over recent weeks. Target is typically < 7.0% for most adults. Glycemic Variability (%CV) Coefficient of Variation reflects how much your glucose swings. A %CV below 36% indicates stable, low-variability glucose control. Ambulatory Glucose Profile (AGP) A standardized 24-hour composite visual curve. The solid line is the 50% median; the dark band represents 50% of days (25th–75th percentile); the light outer band encompasses 80% (10th–90th percentile). Stream vs History vs Scans Stream: live 1-minute Bluetooth values. History: 15-minute values stored inside the sensor memory and backfilled on reconnection. Scans: readings taken by physically holding your phone to the sensor via NFC. Sensor Calibration Guidelines Applies blood glucose fingerprick measurements to calibrate continuous sensor data. Calibrate only when glucose is stable (flat trend arrow), never during fast rises, drops, or immediately after eating. Broadcasts & Integrations Glucodata and xDrip broadcasts send readings locally to watchfaces, widgets, and apps on your device. Local web server serves Nightscout API locally without internet.

DEVELOPMENT & TESTING Side-by-Side Installation & Relay Run a secondary build (e.g., tk.glucodata.dev) side-by-side with production without switching Bluetooth. Production stays connected to the sensor and relays live glucose via Mirror TCP/IP, local broadcast, or local web server. Setup Side-by-Side Mirror Testing Guide Receiver Active (Receiving live data) Sender Active (Relaying data) Standalone / Direct Sensor Side-by-Side Dev Testing Guide Side-by-Side Installation (Different App ID)
Why this is recommended:
Changing the applicationId on your dev build (e.g. tk.glucodata.dev) prevents data corruption or schema collisions from breaking your daily production install.
How to relay live data without switching Bluetooth:
1. Production App (Paired to sensor):
• Keeps the physical Bluetooth connection to the CGM sensor.
• Under Mirror settings, ensure its sync port is active (default 17580 or 8795).
• Or tap \'Configure as Sender\' with target port 17581 to push data to the dev build.
• Alternatively, enable Patched Libre Broadcast (com.librelink.app) or Local xDrip Server.
2. Development Build (tk.glucodata.dev):
• Use a distinct listen port (e.g. 17581) to avoid socket binding collisions on the same device.
• In Mirror Settings, tap Connect as Receiver (Dev Mode) with target IP 127.0.0.1 and target port 17580.
• The dev build will immediately start receiving live readings, stream, and scans from production!
